quick_facts.label: What the job is
quick_facts.value: ASQ (the American Society for Quality) describes a Certified Reliability Engineer as a professional who specialises in improving the reliability, maintainability and safety of products, systems and processes.

quick_facts.label: Related job titles
quick_facts.value: O*NET lists Reliability Engineer among the job titles reported for its Validation Engineers occupation, alongside Quality Engineer and Supplier Quality Engineer.

quick_facts.label: Professional certification
quick_facts.value: ASQ's Certified Reliability Engineer certification asks for eight years of on-the-job experience in its Body of Knowledge areas, three of them in a decision-making position; a bachelor's degree waives four of those years and a master's or doctorate waives five.

sections.heading: What a reliability engineer does
paragraphs: ASQ describes reliability engineers as focused on identifying potential failures, optimising performance, and ensuring compliance with quality and reliability standards.
ASQ is a US-based professional body; the description is of the profession in general rather than of any one company.
bullets: Identify how a product, system or process could fail.
Check compliance with quality and reliability standards.

sections.heading: How people get into this job
paragraphs: In India, the UGC specification of degrees lists B.Tech and B.E. as four-year bachelor's degrees entered after 10+2.

For engineers already working in the field, ASQ offers the Certified Reliability Engineer exam. The computer-delivered version is a one-part, 165-question, open-book exam (150 questions scored) with 4 hours and 18 minutes of exam time.
bullets: Common routes into this job on the Career Tree map: B.Tech in Mechanical Engineering; B.Tech in Electrical Engineering; B.Tech in Electronics and Communication Engineering; Graduate Engineer Trainee; Quality Engineer; Validation Engineer.
